title: Debug phone connection to mobile app host
Review relevant prior worklogs and project context for host connectivity behavior
Inspect host dev scripts and runtime configuration for bind host, port, and advertised URL
Derive likely cause and provide phone/VPN connectivity checks or code/docs fixes if needed

content: Starting by reviewing repo state and prior worklogs that mention host/client connectivity.

observation: Troubleshooting/development should prefer simple solutions and pause for human clarification when blocked by environment-specific behavior.
Use structured worklogs for the session; record meaningful observations and finish/block/cancel tasks before reporting.

Repository is on main with existing local changes in apps/mobile/app.json, apps/mobile/package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, and untracked apps/mobile/ios/. These appear unrelated and should not be touched during connection debugging.

The host defaults to binding localhost on port 4739. Physical phones require a LAN/Tailscale-reachable host URL and PI_MOBILE_HOST_BIND=0.0.0.0. The mobile app default host URL is http://localhost:4739, suitable only for simulator-on-Mac, not a physical phone.
Prior work established host exposes /api/health, /api/host/status and /ws, and mobile client uses HTTP plus WebSocket for live events.
Recent reconnect/path explorer work kept direct LAN/Tailscale workflow and added recent host/session history; no QR pairing or hosted relay exists.

content: Reviewed README and relevant prior worklogs. The project expects direct reachable host URLs for physical devices, while localhost only works from simulator/Mac context.
Inspecting host bootstrap/listen behavior, mobile URL handling, and local network/DNS status for mbp.sgponte:4739.

observation: Host process reads PI_MOBILE_HOST_BIND (default localhost), PI_MOBILE_HOST_PORT (default 4739), optional token, then calls server.listen(port, hostname). With PI_MOBILE_HOST_BIND=0.0.0.0 it should listen on all IPv4 interfaces.

GET /api/health is intentionally unauthenticated and should be the first connectivity test. /api/host/status and /ws require token only when PI_MOBILE_HOST_TOKEN is set; WebSocket token may be provided as /ws?token=.

The mobile client uses the exact Host URL input as fetch base URL and converts http:// to ws:// for live events. It strips trailing slashes but does not append a port or scheme, so the UI must contain a complete URL such as http://mbp.sgponte:4739.
The app currently hardcodes DEFAULT_HOST_URL to http://localhost:4739 in App.tsx; app.json's extra.defaultHostUrl is not used. A physical phone must manually enter or use a saved reachable URL.

When started with PI_MOBILE_HOST_BIND=0.0.0.0 PI_MOBILE_HOST_PORT=4739 pnpm dev:host, lsof shows node listening on TCP *:4739, curl http://127.0.0.1:4739/api/health returns {ok:true}, curl http://mbp.sgponte:4739/api/health returns {ok:true}, and ws://mbp.sgponte:4739/ws returns a host_status event from the Mac.

The generated native iOS Info.plist has NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=false and NSAllowsLocalNetworking=true. If iOS does not classify the Surge Ponte 198.18.x.x hostname as local networking, cleartext http://mbp.sgponte:4739 may be blocked by App Transport Security even when Safari/curl can reach it.

content: Confirmed the host bind and route behavior in code and with a local smoke test. The daemon is reachable at http://mbp.sgponte:4739/api/health and ws://mbp.sgponte:4739/ws from the Mac when bound to 0.0.0.0.
Preparing concise diagnosis and a decision tree for phone-side checks: full URL/port, phone browser health endpoint, iOS ATS/native build behavior, token, firewall/VPN.

Diagnosis ready. Main likely causes are an incomplete/default Host URL in the app, phone/VPN/firewall reachability if the phone cannot load /api/health, or iOS ATS cleartext blocking if Safari can load /api/health but the native app cannot.
